ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a beautiful Pythagorean tree, in which all the quadrilaterals are squares, and all the triangles are right-angled triangles. If the side lengths of squares $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are $3$, $6$, $2$, and $3$ respectively, what is the area of the largest square $E$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,\\
by the Pythagorean theorem, the area of square $F$ is equal to the area of square $A$ plus the area of square $B$ = $3^{2}+6^{2}=45$,\\
Similarly, the area of square $G$ is equal to the area of square $C$ plus the area of square $D$ = $2^{2}+3^{2}=13$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of square $E$ is equal to the area of square $F$ plus the area of square $G$ = $45+13=\boxed{58}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,\\ by the Pythagorean theorem, the area of square $F$ is equal to the area of square $A$ plus the area of square $B$: $3^{2}+6^{2}=45$,\\ Similarly, the area of square $G$ is equal to the area of square $C$ plus the area of square $D$: $2^{2}+3^{2}=13$,\\ $\therefore$ the area of square $E$ is equal to the area of square $F$ plus the area of square $G$: $45+13=\boxed{58}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a Pythagoras tree structure; all quadrilaterals are drawn as squares, and the connections are right triangles. The squares A and B in the upper left are respectively attached to the two legs of the same right triangle, and the hypotenuse of this triangle corresponds to an unnamed tilted square on the middle left, which can be denoted as F. The squares C and D in the upper right are likewise attached to the two legs of another right triangle, and the hypotenuse of this triangle corresponds to the unnamed tilted square on the middle right, which can be denoted as G. Finally, F and G serve as the squares on the two legs of a right triangle below, and the largest square E is on the hypotenuse of this triangle. Then reason: It is known that the side lengths of A, B, C, D are respectively 3, 6, 2, 3. By the area form of the Pythagorean theorem, the area of the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the areas of the squares on the two legs, so area(F)=area(A)+area(B)=3^2+6^2=9+36=45. Similarly, area(G)=area(C)+area(D)=2^2+3^2=4+9=13. The largest square E corresponds to the hypotenuse square with F and G as the squares on the two legs, therefore area(E)=area(F)+area(G)=45+13=58.
